h: Reverence Makes the Kohen a Sanctuary in Every Generation

p: "Speak to the Kohanim, the sons of Aharon,
a parable — to what is the matter comparable?
that you shall not see the dead, etc.,
because you go out and come in, etc.,
so that you not defile my palace.'
So too the Holy One, blessed is He, decreed
upon the Kohanim who enter the Beis HaMikdash
that they not become impure to a dead body."
a prohibition of impurity for Kohanim
except when the Beis HaMikdash stands,
when they enter to perform the service,
Moreover, how would the Kohen defile
If during his days of impurity,
it is forbidden in any case to enter the Mikdash,
הָא כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּזְהָרִין עַל זֶה
all of Yisrael are warned about this.
And once he becomes pure, he is permitted to enter.
And what does it matter that he regularly
When he becomes impure, he will not come,
they were divided into twenty-four watches
and each one offered only on his day
and would not come to the Beis HaMikdash otherwise;
so why may he not become impure then?
He would not be defiling the palace!
And also, how is this an answer
to why the expression of saying is stated
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
according to what they said in the Midrash Rabbah
and so it is in Midrash Tehillim (19:14),
"The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever":
"Through the fear with which Aharon feared
before the Holy One, blessed is He,
'And I gave them to him for fear, and he feared Me'
(as it is expounded in Vayikra Rabbah 3:6),
he merited that this parashah was given to him,
which does not depart from him,
nor from his sons, nor from his sons' sons,
until the end of all generations.
And which is it? The parashah of the dead, etc."
do not apply to the Kohanim
except when the Beis HaMikdash stands,
whereas the impurity of Kohanim applies for all generations,
Yet this needs to be understood:
the prohibition of a divorcee and a zonah
also applies for all generations, forever!
But it appears that he said it as a novelty:
that the prohibition of impurity from the dead,
which stems from his entering the Beis HaMikdash,
as they said in the Tanchuma,
and which ought to have applied
only when the Beis HaMikdash stands
he merited that it should apply
to his sons and his sons' sons forever.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
according to what is written in the holy Zohar
this is the Shabbos of Shabbos eve,
That is: the attribute of Malchus,
"A king whose awe shall be upon you."
"From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed is He,
'The Rock of my heart and my portion
And this is what is said (Bamidbar 35:34),
אֲנִי ה׳ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"I, Hashem, dwell in the midst of Bnei Yisrael":
for the heart is the dwelling place of holiness.
And this is "And My Sanctuary you shall revere."
of whom it is written, "And I gave them to him for fear, and he feared Me,"
that Hashem Yisbarach dwells constantly in his heart,
and he is always in the Mikdash.
Therefore there was forbidden to him and his sons,
until the end of all generations,
impurity of the dead, even nowadays,
for they are always as though in the Mikdash.
And this is "Speak to the Kohanim, etc.,
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, needed
to instill this holiness in them;
just as with the sanctification of firstborns:
although a firstborn is holy of itself,
nevertheless it is a mitzvah to sanctify it
to instill the holiness in the firstborns.
So too the holiness of the Kohanim,
as they are in the Beis HaMikdash
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, needed
as is written in the holy Zohar
to instill the holiness in them,
so that this parashah should apply for all generations,
אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
even when the Beis HaMikdash does not stand.
And this is why he brought this parable,
and nevertheless its prohibition applies forever,
אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
even when the Beis HaMikdash does not stand;
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, needed
to instill the holiness in them.
And on Shabbos all of Yisrael are called
and all of Yisrael are like Kohanim
who are always in the Mikdash;
as is written in the holy Zohar cited above (Introduction 5b):
this is the Shabbos of Shabbos eve,
is like the Mikdash in space.
Only, since it is only on Shabbos
impurity of the dead was not forbidden to them
for so too with the Mikdash itself,
entry of a Yisrael into the Mikdash.
as though they are in the Mikdash,
דִּכְתִיב יִרְאַת ה׳ טְהוֹרָה עוֹמֶדֶת לָעַד
as it is written, "The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever"
And Yisrael on Shabbos are like Kohanim,
for they are free then only for Torah,
as was said to them at Mattan Torah
וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹ׳
"And you shall be to Me a kingdom of Kohanim, etc.";
and as it will be in the future,
וְאַתֶּם כֹּהֲנֵי ה׳ תִּקָּרֵאוּ (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, ו)
"And you shall be called the Kohanim of Hashem" (Yeshayahu 61:6):
for they will then be free only for Torah,
and "Strangers shall stand and tend, etc." (Yeshayahu 61:5).
And about this it says, "And My Sanctuary you shall revere."

Aharon Inherits Holiness Through Lasting Reverence
Moshe Awakens the Holiness Already Within
Shabbos Gives All Yisrael a Priestly Calling
